It allows air to flow from the compressor to the tank, but prevents it from flowing back out. This is a safety device that ensures the air tanks will remain charged even if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: What should you do if you are transporting hazardous materials and you get into an accident?
answers: Stop, secure the scene, and keep people away from the vehicle.
Try to clean up the spill yourself.
Leave the scene to avoid getting in trouble.
Do not tell anyone that you are carrying hazardous materials.
feedbacks: Correct: Your first priority is to prevent anyone from being injured by the hazardous material.
Incorrect: You should not attempt to clean up a hazardous materials spill unless you are trained and equipped to do so.
Incorrect: This is illegal and extremely dangerous.
Incorrect: You must inform emergency responders about the hazardous materials so they can take the proper precautions.
questions.explanation: If you have an accident while transporting hazardous materials, your top priority is to protect yourself and the public. You should stop in a safe place, keep people away from the scene, and notify the proper authorities. You should also have your shipping papers ready to give to emergency responders.

questions.question: What are some of the things you should inspect on the outside of a bus?
answers: The tires and wheels.
The lights and reflectors.
The emergency exits.
The paint job.
feedbacks: Correct: This is a critical safety check for any vehicle.
Correct: All lights and reflectors must be clean and working.
Correct: You must make sure that all emergency exits are clearly marked and can be opened easily.
Incorrect: The condition of the paint is not a safety item.
questions.explanation: When inspecting the outside of a bus, you should pay special attention to the items that are critical for safety. This includes the tires, wheels, lights, reflectors, mirrors, windows, and all emergency exits.

questions.question: What is the '50% rule' for cargo securement?
answers: The aggregate working load limit of all tie-downs must be at least 50% of the weight of the cargo.
You must secure at least 50% of the items in your load.
You can only fill your trailer to 50% of its capacity.
You should spend at least 50% of your pre-trip inspection checking your cargo.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the fundamental rule of cargo securement.
Incorrect: You must secure the entire load.
Incorrect: This is not a rule.
Incorrect: There is no time requirement for this.
questions.explanation: The '50% rule' is a shorthand way of saying that the combined strength of all your cargo securement devices must be at least half of the weight of the cargo you are carrying. This is to ensure that the cargo will stay in place during normal driving conditions.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 'Class A', 'Class B', and 'Class C' CDL?
answers: The class of CDL you need depends on the gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of the vehicle you will be driving and the weight of the trailer you will be towing.
Class A is for trucks, Class B is for buses, and Class C is for cars.
Class A is the hardest to get, and Class C is the easiest.
You must get a Class C before you can get a Class B, and a Class B before you can get a Class A.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the primary distinction between the classes.
Incorrect: The classes are based on weight, not vehicle type.
Incorrect: The difficulty of obtaining the license depends on the individual.
Incorrect: You can apply for any class of license if you meet the qualifications.
questions.explanation: The class of CDL that you need is determined by the weight of the vehicle you will be driving. A Class A CDL is for combination vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 lbs. or more, where the towed unit has a GVWR of over 10,000 lbs. A Class B CDL is for single vehicles with a GVWR of 26,001 lbs. or more, or a combination vehicle where the towed unit has a GVWR of 10,000 lbs. or less. A Class C CDL is for vehicles that do not meet the criteria for a Class A or B, but are designed to transport 16 or more passengers or are placarded for hazardous materials.

questions.question: What are the two main things to look for when inspecting your tires?
answers: Proper inflation and tread depth.
The brand and the size.
If they are clean and shiny.
If they are new or used.
feedbacks: Correct: These are the two most critical aspects of tire safety.
Incorrect: The brand is not important, and the size should already be correct for the vehicle.
Incorrect: Cleanliness is not a safety factor.
Incorrect: A used tire can be safe if it is in good condition.
questions.explanation: The two most important things to check on your tires during a pre-trip inspection are the inflation pressure and the tread depth. Under-inflated tires and worn-out tires are two of the leading causes of tire failure.

questions.question: What is the 'space cushion' you should maintain around your vehicle?
answers: The space ahead of you, behind you, and to your sides.
The space inside your cab.
The space between your vehicle and the curb.
The space under your vehicle.
feedbacks: Correct: You should always be surrounded by a cushion of space.
Incorrect: The space cushion is outside the vehicle.
Incorrect: This is part of the space cushion, but not the whole thing.
Incorrect: This is your ground clearance.
questions.explanation: A space cushion is the area of open space that you maintain around your vehicle. It gives you room to maneuver and time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You should manage the space ahead of you, behind you, and on both sides of your vehicle.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the safety valve on an air tank?
answers: It protects the tank from being over-pressurized by releasing air if the pressure gets too high.
It is a valve that you use to drain the water from the tank.
It is a valve that keeps the air in the tank from leaking out.
It is a valve that allows you to fill the tank with air.
feedbacks: Correct: It is a safety device to prevent the tank from rupturing.
Incorrect: This is the drain valve.
Incorrect: This is the function of the check valve.
Incorrect: The compressor fills the tank.
questions.explanation: The safety valve on an air tank is designed to pop open automatically if the air pressure gets too high (usually around 150 psi). This is to prevent the tank from exploding. If the safety valve releases air, it means there is a problem with the air compressor governor and it should be repaired.

questions.question: What is a 'combustible' liquid?
answers: A liquid that has a flash point at or above 100°F (37.8°C).
A liquid that will not burn.
A liquid that is safe to transport without a placard.
A liquid that is used in a comb.
feedbacks: Correct: Combustible liquids are less flammable than 'flammable' liquids, but still pose a fire hazard.
Incorrect: Combustible liquids will burn.
Incorrect: A placard is required if you are transporting more than 119 gallons of a combustible liquid.
Incorrect: This is not a real term.
questions.explanation: A combustible liquid is a liquid that will burn, but is not as easily ignited as a flammable liquid. The DOT defines a combustible liquid as any liquid that has a flash point at or above 100°F and below 200°F. Diesel fuel is an example of a combustible liquid.

questions.question: What are some of the things that a school bus driver must do at a railroad crossing?
answers: Stop, open the door and window, and listen and look for a train.
Slow down and look both ways.
Stop and honk the horn.
Stop and activate the flashing red lights.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the complete and required procedure.
Incorrect: A full stop is required.
Incorrect: Honking the horn is not part of the procedure.
Incorrect: You activate the four-way hazard lights, not the red flashing lights used for loading and unloading.
questions.explanation: The driver of a school bus must bring the bus to a complete stop at all railroad crossings. They must then open the service door and their window, and listen and look in both directions for any sign of an approaching train. Only when it is clear and safe to do so can they proceed across the tracks.

questions.question: What is the proper way to secure a load of logs?
answers: With at least two tie-downs.
With one tie-down for every 10 feet of logs.
The tie-downs must be made of chain.
The logs must be loaded with the bark side down.
feedbacks: Correct: Logs require special securement due to their shape and weight.
Correct: The number of tie-downs depends on the length of the logs.
Incorrect: Straps can be used if they have the proper working load limit.
Incorrect: This is not a requirement.
questions.explanation: A load of logs must be secured with at least two tie-downs. For logs longer than 10 feet, you need one tie-down for the first 10 feet and an additional tie-down for each additional 10 feet or fraction thereof. The tie-downs must be arranged to prevent the logs from rolling or shifting.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 'CDL' and an 'operator's license'?
answers: A CDL is required to operate commercial motor vehicles, while an operator's license is for personal vehicles.
A CDL is harder to get than an operator's license.
A CDL is a federal license, while an operator's license is a state license.
There is no difference.
feedbacks: Correct: They are for two different classes of vehicles.
Correct: It requires more testing and a higher level of knowledge and skill.
Incorrect: Both are issued by the state, but the CDL is regulated by the federal government.
Incorrect: They are very different.
questions.explanation: A Commercial Driver's License (CDL) is a special license that is required to operate vehicles that are large, heavy, or are used to transport hazardous materials or a large number of passengers. An operator's license, or a standard driver's license, is for personal, non-commercial vehicles. The testing and qualification standards for a CDL are much stricter than for an operator's license.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for tires on a commercial vehicle (other than the front tires)?
answers: 1/32 of an inch.
2/32 of an inch.
4/32 of an inch.
6/32 of an inch.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is too low.
Correct: This is the federal minimum.
Incorrect: This is the minimum for front tires.
Incorrect: This is a recommended depth for good traction, but not the legal minimum.
questions.explanation: The FMCSA regulations require that all tires on a commercial motor vehicle, other than the front steering tires, have a tread depth of at least 2/32 of an inch. The tread depth must be measured in any two adjacent major tread grooves at the lowest point of the tread.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signal?
answers: At least 100 feet before you make the turn.
Just as you begin to make the turn.
Only when there are other vehicles around.
You don't need to use your turn signal if you are in a turn-only lane.
feedbacks: Correct: This gives other drivers enough warning of your intentions.
Incorrect: This does not give other drivers enough time to react.
Incorrect: You should always use your turn signal, even if you don't see any other vehicles.
Incorrect: You must still signal your turn.
questions.explanation: You should signal your intention to turn at least 100 feet before you make the turn. This is about 4-5 car lengths. In a large truck, you should signal even earlier to give other drivers plenty of warning.

questions.question: What is the 'air governor'?
answers: It is a device that controls the air compressor, telling it when to pump air and when to stop.
It is a device that governs the speed of the vehicle.
It is a device that controls the temperature of the air in the cab.
It is a person who is in charge of the air brakes.
feedbacks: Correct: It maintains the air pressure in the system within a set range.
Incorrect: This is a speed governor.
Incorrect: This is the climate control system.
Incorrect: The driver is in charge of the air brakes.
questions.explanation: The air governor controls the operation of the air compressor. It is set to a 'cut-in' pressure (usually around 100 psi) and a 'cut-out' pressure (usually around 125 psi). When the air pressure drops to the cut-in level, the governor tells the compressor to start pumping air. When the pressure reaches the cut-out level, the governor tells the compressor to stop.

questions.question: What is the difference between a 'label' and a 'placard' for hazardous materials?
answers: A label is a smaller diamond-shaped sticker that is placed on the package, while a placard is a larger diamond-shaped sign that is placed on the vehicle.
A label is for flammable materials, and a placard is for corrosive materials.
A label is optional, but a placard is required.
There is no difference.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the primary difference between the two.
Incorrect: Both labels and placards are used for all classes of hazardous materials.
Incorrect: Both are required under certain circumstances.
Incorrect: They are two different things with different requirements.
questions.explanation: A label is a small, diamond-shaped warning that is put on the individual packages of hazardous materials. A placard is a larger, diamond-shaped sign that is put on the outside of the vehicle to indicate that it is carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: What is the 'no-zone'?
answers: The large blind spots around a truck or bus.
A zone where you are not allowed to drive a truck.
A zone where there is no cell phone service.
A zone where the speed limit is zero.
feedbacks: Correct: These are the areas where the driver cannot see other vehicles.
Incorrect: It is an area around the truck.
Incorrect: It is not related to cell service.
Incorrect: This is not a real thing.
questions.explanation: The 'no-zone' is a term used to describe the large blind spots around a commercial motor vehicle. These blind spots are on all four sides of the vehicle, and cars that are driving in the no-zone cannot be seen by the truck driver. It is important for both truck drivers and other motorists to be aware of the no-zone and to avoid it.

questions.question: What is the proper way to secure a load of heavy equipment?
answers: With at least four tie-downs, one at each corner of the equipment.
With one tie-down over the top of the equipment.
By driving it onto the trailer and setting the parking brake.
With ropes and bungee cords.
feedbacks: Correct: Heavy equipment must be secured at multiple points to prevent it from shifting.
Incorrect: This is not enough to secure a heavy piece of equipment.
Incorrect: The equipment must be tied down.
Incorrect: You must use properly rated chains and binders.
questions.explanation: Heavy equipment, such as a bulldozer or a backhoe, must be secured with at least four tie-downs, each with a working load limit of at least 5,000 pounds. The tie-downs should be attached at the front and rear corners of the equipment to prevent it from moving in any direction. Any accessories, such as a bucket or a blade, must also be lowered and secured.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out while you are driving?
answers: Brake hard and steer straight.
Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed down.
Accelerate to try to maintain control.
Immediately pull over to the side of the road.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Braking hard can cause you to lose control.
Correct: This is the proper procedure for handling a blowout.
Incorrect: This can make the situation worse.
Incorrect: You should slow down gradually before pulling over.
questions.explanation: If you have a tire blowout, you should hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the accelerator. Do not brake, as this could cause the vehicle to skid. Let the vehicle slow down on its own, and then gently brake and pull over to a safe location.

questions.question: What is a 'controlled intersection'?
answers: An intersection with traffic lights or signs.
An intersection that is controlled by a police officer.
An intersection with no signs or signals.
An intersection that is very busy.
feedbacks: Correct: These devices control the flow of traffic.
Correct: A police officer's directions override all other traffic controls.
Incorrect: This is an uncontrolled intersection.
Incorrect: The amount of traffic does not determine if it is controlled.
questions.explanation: A controlled intersection is one where traffic is regulated by traffic signals, stop signs, or yield signs. An intersection can also be controlled by a law enforcement officer, and in that case, you must follow the officer's directions, even if they are different from the traffic signals.

questions.question: How can you avoid a rear-end collision?
answers: By maintaining a safe following distance.
By watching the brake lights of the vehicle in front of you.
By driving faster than the vehicle in front of you.
By looking in your mirrors frequently.
feedbacks: Correct: This gives you more time to stop.
Correct: This is a good way to anticipate when they are going to slow down or stop.
Incorrect: This will decrease your following distance and increase your risk.
Incorrect: While a good practice, this does not directly prevent a rear-end collision with the vehicle in front of you.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid hitting the vehicle in front of you is to maintain a safe following distance. You should also pay close attention to the traffic ahead and be prepared to stop if necessary. Watching the brake lights of the vehicle in front of you, and even the vehicle in front of them, can give you an early warning that traffic is slowing down.

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'baffles' in a tanker?
answers: To help control the forward and backward surge of the liquid.
To keep different types of liquids separated.
To clean the inside of the tanker.
To make the tanker stronger.
feedbacks: Correct: Baffles are partitions that slow down the movement of the liquid.
Incorrect: These are called bulkheads.
Incorrect: The tanker must be cleaned by other means.
Incorrect: The baffles are not a structural component.
questions.explanation: Baffles are walls inside a tanker that have holes in them to allow the liquid to flow through. Their purpose is to slow down the sloshing or 'surge' of the liquid from front to back, which makes the vehicle more stable. They do not prevent side-to-side surge.

questions.question: When are you allowed to use a cell phone while driving a commercial vehicle?
answers: Whenever you want.
Only when you are using a hands-free device.
Only when you are stopped at a red light.
Never.
feedbacks: Incorrect: There are strict regulations on cell phone use.
Correct: In most cases, you can use a hands-free phone, but even that is discouraged.
Incorrect: You are still considered to be driving when you are stopped in traffic.
Incorrect: Hands-free use is generally permitted, though some companies may have stricter policies.
questions.explanation: The FMCSA regulations prohibit commercial drivers from using a hand-held mobile telephone while driving. This includes reaching for, holding, or dialing a phone. A driver is allowed to use a hands-free phone, but they must be able to activate it with a single button press. Even with a hands-free device, it is still a distraction and should be used with extreme caution.

questions.question: What are some of the things you should do to prepare for driving in the winter?
answers: Check the weather forecast before you leave.
Make sure your vehicle is in good condition, with good tires, brakes, and a full tank of fuel.
Bring extra warm clothing, food, and water.
Drive faster to get to your destination sooner.
feedbacks: Correct: This will help you to anticipate any bad weather.
Correct: A well-maintained vehicle is essential for winter driving.
Correct: You should be prepared in case you get stranded.
Incorrect: You should slow down in winter conditions.
questions.explanation: Winter driving requires special preparation. You should always check the weather forecast, make sure your vehicle is in top condition, and carry an emergency kit with warm clothes, food, and water. You should also adjust your driving to the conditions by slowing down and increasing your following distance.

questions.question: What is a 'tandem axle'?
answers: Two axles that are spaced close together.
An axle that can be raised and lowered.
An axle that is not connected to the engine.
An axle that has four wheels.
feedbacks: Correct: They are treated as a single unit for weight limit purposes.
Incorrect: This is a lift axle.
Incorrect: This is a dead axle.
Incorrect: This is a dual axle.
questions.explanation: A tandem axle is a set of two or more consecutive axles that are spaced more than 40 inches apart but not more than 96 inches apart. For the purpose of weight limits, a tandem axle is considered a single unit.

questions.question: What should you do if you are being tailgated?
answers: Brake suddenly to get the other driver to back off.
Increase your following distance from the vehicle in front of you.
Speed up to get away from the tailgater.
Get out of your vehicle and confront the other driver.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This could cause them to hit you.
Correct: This will give you more room to stop and will encourage the tailgater to pass you.
Incorrect: This could make the situation more dangerous.
Incorrect: This could lead to a road rage incident.
questions.explanation: If you are being tailgated, the safest thing to do is to increase your own following distance. This will give you and the tailgater more time to stop if necessary. You should also avoid any sudden moves and, if possible, move to another lane to let the tailgater pass.

questions.question: What are the two main types of cargo?
answers: Bulk and packaged.
Heavy and light.
Liquid and solid.
Hazardous and non-hazardous.
feedbacks: Correct: This is a common way to classify cargo.
Incorrect: This is a description of the cargo, not a type.
Incorrect: This is a physical state, not a type of cargo.
Incorrect: This is a classification of the cargo, not a type.
questions.explanation: Cargo is generally classified as either bulk or packaged. Bulk cargo is a commodity that is transported unpackaged in large quantities, such as grain, coal, or oil. Packaged cargo is cargo that is shipped in boxes, barrels, or other containers.

questions.question: What is the '11-hour rule' for property-carrying drivers?
answers: A driver can drive for a maximum of 11 hours after 10 consecutive hours off duty.
A driver must take an 11-hour break after every shift.
A driver can work for 11 hours, but only 8 of those can be driving hours.
A driver can drive for 11 consecutive hours without a break.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the driving limit within the 14-hour window.
Incorrect: The required break is 10 hours.
Incorrect: The driving limit is 11 hours.
Incorrect: A 30-minute break is required after 8 hours of driving.
questions.explanation: The 11-hour rule states that a driver of a property-carrying CMV can drive for a maximum of 11 hours within a 14-consecutive-hour period, after having had at least 10 consecutive hours off duty.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'pre-cooling' a reefer unit?
answers: To cool the trailer down before loading the cargo.
To cool the engine before starting it.
To cool the brakes before going down a hill.
To cool the driver before they get in the cab.
feedbacks: Correct: This helps to maintain the proper temperature of the cargo.
Incorrect: The engine does not need to be pre-cooled.
Incorrect: Brakes are cooled by air, not a reefer unit.
Incorrect: The cab has its own air conditioning.
questions.explanation: A refrigerated trailer, or 'reefer', should be pre-cooled to the desired temperature before the cargo is loaded. This is to ensure that the cargo, which should already be at the correct temperature, does not warm up while it is being loaded.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'fifth wheel'?
answers: It is the coupling device that connects the tractor to the semi-trailer.
It is a spare tire.
It is the fifth wheel on the vehicle.
It is a brand of trailer.
feedbacks: Correct: It is a critical component of a combination vehicle.
Incorrect: The spare tire is separate.
Incorrect: A tractor-trailer has many more than five wheels.
Incorrect: It is a part of the tractor.
questions.explanation: The fifth wheel is a large, round plate on the back of the tractor that has a locking mechanism to connect with the kingpin of the semi-trailer. It is a very strong and secure connection that allows the combination vehicle to pivot when turning.

questions.question: As of 2025, what is a key change in the FMCSA's drug testing panel for CDL drivers?
answers: Inclusion of oral fluid testing as an alternative to urine testing.
Removal of marijuana from the testing panel.
Testing is now only required after an accident.
Drivers can now refuse one random test per year without penalty.
feedbacks: Correct: The FMCSA has authorized oral fluid testing as an additional approved method, which can be used in various testing situations.
Incorrect: Marijuana (specifically THC metabolites) remains a substance tested for under DOT regulations.
Incorrect: Pre-employment, random, post-accident, and reasonable suspicion testing are all still required.
Incorrect: Refusing a test is treated as a failed test and results in immediate disqualification.
questions.explanation: In 2023, the DOT published a final rule authorizing the use of oral fluid specimens for drug testing, with implementation occurring over the following months into 2025. This provides employers with an alternative to urine testing for all required drug tests.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection on a combination vehicle, you check the trailer's landing gear. Which TWO of the following are major defects?
answers: The landing gear is fully raised.
The crank handle is missing.
The landing gear support frame is severely bent or cracked.
The landing gear feet are dirty.
The landing gear has minor surface rust.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The landing gear should be fully raised after coupling for normal operation.
Correct: A missing crank handle prevents the landing gear from being raised or lowered, which is a critical function.
Correct: Structural damage to the support frame can lead to a collapse of the landing gear and the trailer.
Incorrect: Dirt or mud on the feet is a minor issue and does not constitute a major defect.
Incorrect: Surface rust is common and not a structural defect unless it is causing deep pitting or holes.
questions.explanation: The landing gear must be structurally sound and fully operational. A missing crank handle renders it inoperable, and a damaged support frame creates a risk of collapse, both of which are serious safety defects.

questions.question: You are driving a tanker at night and need to make an emergency stop. The tanker is half-full of a flammable liquid. What is the most significant risk specific to this situation?
answers: The high center of gravity will cause an immediate rollover.
The liquid surge could push the truck forward or sideways, making it harder to control.
The headlights will fail due to the sudden stop.
The flammable liquid will ignite from the heat of the brakes.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While the center of gravity is high, it's the liquid's movement that is the most immediate, unique risk here.
Correct: The 'slosh' effect in a partially loaded tanker is magnified during sudden maneuvers like an emergency stop, severely impacting stability.
Incorrect: A sudden stop should not cause the headlights to fail.
Incorrect: While brake heat is a concern, ignition is not the most significant and immediate risk from the stop itself compared to the loss of control from surge.
questions.explanation: In a partially loaded tanker without baffles (a smoothbore tanker), liquid surge is a powerful force. During an emergency stop, the momentum of the sloshing liquid can destabilize the vehicle, making a jackknife or rollover more likely.

questions.question: Under the HOS 30-minute break rule, which of the following activities is allowed during the break?
answers: Performing fueling or other on-duty tasks.
Eating a meal in the sleeper berth.
Completing your daily logbook.
Waiting in line to load or unload at a customer's facility.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The break must be 'off-duty' or 'sleeper berth' status.
Correct: A driver is relieved of all responsibility and can be in 'off-duty' or 'sleeper berth' status.
Incorrect: This is considered on-duty, not-driving work.
Incorrect: This is 'on-duty, not-driving' unless the driver is released from all responsibility for the vehicle.
questions.explanation: The 30-minute break, required after 8 hours of cumulative driving, must be recorded as 'Off Duty' or 'Sleeper Berth'. The driver must be relieved of all work-related duties during this time. Eating in the sleeper berth qualifies as a valid break.

questions.question: While descending a steep grade, you are in the proper low gear and your brakes are working normally. What is the correct braking technique to use?
answers: Apply the brakes continuously but lightly all the way down the grade.
Apply the brakes firmly to a complete stop every quarter mile to cool them.
Apply the brakes just hard enough to feel a definite slowdown, release when 5 mph below your safe speed, and repeat as needed.
Pump the brake pedal in short, rapid bursts.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This leads to brake fade from constant heat buildup.
Incorrect: Stopping in the middle of a steep downgrade is impractical and dangerous.
Correct: This is the 'snub braking' technique, which allows brakes to cool between applications.
Incorrect: This is an inefficient way to brake with an air brake system and does not manage heat effectively.
questions.explanation: The proper technique for controlling speed on a downgrade, known as 'snub braking', involves applying firm pressure to slow the vehicle down significantly, then releasing the brakes to let them cool. This prevents overheating and brake fade. See FMCSA CDL Manual Section 2.

questions.question: Your air compressor has a cut-out pressure of 125 psi and a cut-in pressure of 100 psi. Your low-pressure warning alarm MUST activate before the pressure drops below what level?
answers: 100 psi
90 psi
55 psi
45 psi
feedbacks: Incorrect: The alarm must go off well before the compressor is scheduled to cut in.
Incorrect: The warning needs to provide an earlier alert than this.
Correct: FMCSA regulations state the low-pressure warning must activate at or above 55 psi (or half the governor cutout on older vehicles).
Incorrect: At this pressure, the spring brakes may already be starting to apply, making it too late for a warning.
questions.explanation: According to FMCSA §393.51, the low-pressure warning system (light and/or buzzer) must activate when air pressure drops to a level between 75 and 55 psi. This gives the driver adequate warning to stop the vehicle safely before the spring brakes begin to engage.

questions.question: A school bus is stopped on a divided highway with its red lights flashing. A car is traveling on the opposite side of the highway. What is the car driver required to do in most states?
answers: Stop and wait for the lights to stop flashing.
Slow down to 10 mph and proceed with caution.
Proceed with caution, as they do not need to stop.
Make a U-turn to avoid the bus.
feedbacks: Incorrect: On a divided highway, traffic in the opposite direction is usually not required to stop.
Incorrect: This specific speed is not a standard rule.
Correct: If the highway is separated by a physical median or an unpaved space, traffic on the opposite side is generally not required to stop.
Incorrect: This would be an illegal and dangerous maneuver.
questions.explanation: Most state laws differentiate between an undivided road and a divided highway. For a school bus stopped on a divided highway, oncoming traffic on the other side of the median is not required to stop, but should still proceed with caution.

questions.question: You are assigned to transport a mixed load of hazardous materials, including Class 1.1 Explosives and Class 8 Corrosive materials. What is the rule for loading these together?
answers: They can be loaded together as long as they are on opposite ends of the trailer.
They must not be loaded, transported, or stored together in the same vehicle.
They can be loaded together if the corrosive material is in a sealed, leak-proof container.
They can be loaded together if you have a special permit from the shipper.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Distance alone is not sufficient; they are incompatible.
Correct: The DOT Segregation Table prohibits loading explosives and corrosives together.
Incorrect: The packaging does not override the segregation rule.
Incorrect: A shipper cannot authorize a violation of federal safety regulations.
questions.explanation: According to the Segregation Table for Hazardous Materials (49 CFR §177.848), Explosives (Class 1.1) and Corrosives (Class 8) are incompatible and must not be transported in the same vehicle due to the risk of a dangerous reaction.

questions.question: What is the new FMCSA requirement for rear impact guards that was phased in through 2024 and is standard for 2025 models?
answers: They must be painted with reflective red and white tape.
They must be strong enough to withstand an impact from a passenger car traveling at 35 mph without significant underride.
They must include a system that automatically lowers the guard closer to the ground when the vehicle is in motion.
They must be made of aluminum to save weight.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This has been a long-standing requirement for conspicuity.
Correct: The new rule, inspired by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, increases the strength requirement from the previous 30 mph standard.
Incorrect: This is a technology that exists but is not part of the federal mandate.
Incorrect: The rule is performance-based and does not specify materials.
questions.explanation: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) issued a final rule strengthening the requirements for rear impact guards on new trailers and semi-trailers. The rule requires guards to provide sufficient strength and energy absorption to protect occupants of a compact or subcompact passenger car impacting the rear of the trailer at 35 mph.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are required to be on a shipping paper for a hazardous materials shipment?
answers: The driver's CDL number.
The proper shipping name and hazard class of the material.
A 24-hour emergency response telephone number.
The name of the shipper.
The vehicle's license plate number.
The price of the hazardous material.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The driver's personal license number is not required on the shipping paper.
Correct: This is fundamental information required to identify the material and its primary danger.
Correct: This number must be monitored at all times the material is in transport, by a person knowledgeable about the material.
Correct: The shipper's name and address are required to identify the origin of the shipment.
Incorrect: Vehicle information is not a required part of the shipping paper itself.
Incorrect: The commercial value of the cargo is not required for safety purposes.
questions.explanation: According to 49 CFR §172.202, a shipping paper must include several key pieces of information, but the most critical are the proper shipping name, hazard class, UN/NA identification number, packing group, total quantity, shipper's information, and an emergency response phone number.

questions.question: You are driving a Class B straight truck in New York City. What is a key rule you must be aware of that might differ from rural driving?
answers: You are exempt from pre-trip inspections in the city.
Many parkways and bridges have specific commercial vehicle restrictions, including lower height and weight limits.
The hours of service rules are suspended within city limits.
You are allowed to use your engine brake at any time to slow down.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Pre-trip inspections are always mandatory.
Correct: NYC has a complex network of roads with strict restrictions for commercial vehicles that drivers must know.
Incorrect: Federal HOS rules apply everywhere.
Incorrect: Many municipalities, including parts of NYC, have restrictions on the use of engine compression brakes due to noise.
questions.explanation: Driving a commercial vehicle in a dense urban environment like New York City requires knowledge of local restrictions. Many roads, especially older parkways, were not designed for modern trucks and have strict height, weight, and length restrictions that are heavily enforced.

questions.question: You are inspecting your suspension system. You notice that one of the leaf springs in a spring stack is cracked. What is the correct action to take?
answers: It's acceptable to drive as long as it's only one spring.
The vehicle must be placed out-of-service until the spring is replaced.
You can continue driving but should make a note to get it fixed at your destination.
You can wrap the cracked spring with heavy-duty tape as a temporary repair.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A cracked leaf spring is a serious safety defect.
Correct: According to the CVSA Out-of-Service Criteria, any broken main leaf spring is an OOS violation.
Incorrect: The vehicle is not safe to operate with this defect.
Incorrect: This is not an acceptable or safe repair method.
questions.explanation: A broken or cracked leaf spring compromises the vehicle's suspension, which can affect steering, braking, and stability. The CVSA Out-of-Service Criteria state that a vehicle with a broken main leaf spring is unsafe and must be placed out-of-service.

questions.question: During an alley dock maneuver, you realize you are about to hit the cone on the passenger side. What is the BEST corrective action?
answers: Turn the steering wheel sharply to the right.
Pull straight forward a few feet to straighten out and then restart the backing maneuver.
Ask the examiner to move the cone for you.
Continue backing slowly and hope you miss it.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This will likely cause the rear of the trailer to swing even wider to the right, hitting the cone.
Correct: Using a 'pull-up' is the safest way to correct your angle and avoid an accident.
Incorrect: You are being tested on your ability to maneuver around fixed objects.
Incorrect: Hope is not a strategy; you must take corrective action.
questions.explanation: When you realize your backing path is incorrect, the safest and most effective solution is to stop, pull forward to straighten the tractor and trailer, and then reassess your approach. This is known as a 'pull-up' and is an essential skill.

questions.question: Your air brake system is fully charged. You turn off the engine, release the service brakes, and time the air pressure drop for one minute. The pressure drops by 4 psi. What does this indicate?
answers: The system is operating perfectly.
There is a leak in the air brake system that needs to be repaired.
The air compressor is not working.
The parking brake is not holding.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This air loss is excessive for a combination vehicle.
Correct: For a combination vehicle, the static air loss rate should be no more than 3 psi per minute.
Incorrect: This test is performed with the engine off, so the compressor is not a factor.
Incorrect: This test is for the air system, not the mechanical holding power of the parking brake.
questions.explanation: This scenario describes the static air leakage test. According to FMCSA §393.51, the maximum allowable air loss for a combination vehicle with the engine off and brakes released is 3 psi in one minute. A 4 psi drop indicates an unacceptable leak.

questions.question: A parent wishes to have their child's large musical instrument (a cello) transported on the school bus. What is the correct procedure?
answers: The instrument can be placed in the aisle if it is tied down.
The instrument can be transported only if it can be held on the student's lap or stowed securely under the seat.
The driver should refuse to transport the instrument under any circumstances.
The instrument can be placed in an empty seat next to the student.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The aisle must be kept clear at all times for safety and emergency evacuation.
Correct: Any object brought onto the bus must not take up a seat or block the aisle or any emergency exits.
Incorrect: It can be transported if it can be done safely and without obstructing anything.
Incorrect: Objects are not allowed to take up seating space intended for passengers.
questions.explanation: School bus safety rules require that aisles and emergency exits remain completely clear. Any object a student brings on board must be small enough to be held in their lap or stowed under their seat without extending into the aisle.

questions.question: You are transporting a load of doubles. Which trailer should generally be the heavier one?
answers: The rear trailer.
The front trailer.
Both trailers should be the exact same weight.
It does not matter which trailer is heavier.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Placing the heavier trailer in the rear creates a 'crack-the-whip' effect and increases the risk of rollover.
Correct: The heavier trailer should always be the one closest to the tractor for maximum stability.
Incorrect: While ideal, this is often not possible. The key is to put the heavier one first.
Incorrect: The placement of weight is critical for the safe handling of doubles.
questions.explanation: When pulling doubles or triples, the heaviest trailer must be the first one behind the tractor. The lightest trailer should always be at the very end. This configuration provides the most stability and reduces the 'crack-the-whip' effect, which can easily cause the rear trailer to roll over.

questions.question: Which TWO of the following actions should you take when driving at night?
answers: Keep your instrument panel lights as bright as possible.
Drive at a slower speed than you would during the day.
Use your high beams whenever it is legal and safe to do so.
Wear sunglasses to reduce glare from oncoming headlights.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Bright interior lights constrict your pupils and make it harder to see outside the vehicle.
Correct: Your visibility is reduced at night, so you need more time to react to hazards.
Correct: High beams can double your field of vision, but you must dim them for other drivers.
Incorrect: Sunglasses reduce the amount of light reaching your eyes, making it even harder to see at night.
questions.explanation: Safe night driving requires adjusting to lower visibility. This means reducing your speed to ensure your stopping distance is within the range of your headlights and using high beams to see farther whenever you are not near other vehicles. Keeping interior lights dim helps your eyes adjust to the darkness outside.

questions.question: You are performing the applied air brake leak test. With the engine off, you apply full pressure to the brake pedal. What is the maximum acceptable pressure drop in one minute for a combination vehicle?
answers: 2 psi
3 psi
4 psi
5 psi
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the limit for a static test on a single vehicle.
Incorrect: This is the limit for a static test on a combination vehicle.
Correct: With the brakes applied, the maximum allowable leak rate for a combination vehicle is 4 psi per minute.
Incorrect: This amount of leakage is considered excessive and unsafe.
questions.explanation: The applied air brake leakage test checks for leaks when the brakes are engaged. For a combination vehicle, after the initial pressure drop, the air pressure should not fall by more than 4 psi in one minute. Any greater loss indicates a leak that must be repaired. See FMCSA CDL Manual Section 5.

questions.question: You are transporting a placarded load of Class 4.2 (Spontaneously Combustible) materials. Which of the following is a primary risk?
answers: The material can explode if it gets wet.
The material is extremely cold and can cause frostbite.
The material can ignite on its own simply by coming into contact with air.
The material is highly corrosive to steel.
feedbacks: Incorrect: That describes a Class 4.3 (Dangerous When Wet) material.
Incorrect: That describes a cryogenic liquid (Class 2.2).
Correct: This is the defining characteristic of a spontaneously combustible material.
Incorrect: That describes a Class 8 material.
questions.explanation: Class 4.2 materials are solids that are liable to spontaneously heat up and ignite when exposed to air. They do not need an external ignition source like a spark or flame to start burning. This makes them particularly dangerous to transport.

questions.question: In Texas, what is a specific requirement for a CDL holder regarding traffic offenses?
answers: You are allowed one speeding ticket per year without it appearing on your record.
You must notify your employer within 30 days of any conviction for a traffic violation, except for parking.
You can take a defensive driving course to dismiss any moving violation.
You only have to report violations that occurred in your commercial vehicle.
feedbacks: Incorrect: All traffic convictions for a CDL holder are recorded.
Correct: Texas law, in alignment with federal law (§383.31), requires drivers to report all traffic convictions (in any type of vehicle) to their employer.
Incorrect: CDL holders are generally not eligible to take defensive driving to dismiss tickets received in any vehicle.
Incorrect: You must report violations that occurred in your personal vehicle as well.
questions.explanation: Both federal and Texas state regulations require a CDL holder to notify their employer of any traffic conviction within 30 days. This applies to violations in any vehicle, commercial or personal. Failure to do so can result in suspension of the CDL.

questions.question: You are inspecting your fuel tank. Which THREE of the following items should you check?
answers: The security of the tank and its mounting brackets.
Any leaks from the tank or fuel lines.
The fuel cap is present and securely fastened.
The brand of the fuel tank.
The color of the fuel tank.
The amount of fuel in the tank is exactly full.
feedbacks: Correct: The fuel tank must be securely attached to the vehicle.
Correct: Fuel leaks are a major fire hazard.
Correct: A missing or loose fuel cap can lead to fuel spillage and contamination.
Incorrect: The manufacturer's brand is irrelevant to a pre-trip inspection.
Incorrect: The color of the tank is not a safety item.
Incorrect: You should check that you have enough fuel for your trip, but it does not need to be completely full.
questions.explanation: The fuel system inspection is a critical part of a pre-trip check. You must ensure the tank is securely mounted, there are no leaks from the tank or lines, and the cap is on tight to prevent spills and fire hazards.

questions.question: A school bus driver is responsible for checking for sleeping children on the bus. What is the MOST effective procedure to ensure the bus is empty?
answers: Honk the horn before leaving the bus to wake any sleeping children.
Walk to the back of the bus after every route, checking under all the seats.
Ask the last student off the bus if anyone else is still on board.
Install a mirror that allows you to see the entire bus from the driver's seat.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a reliable method.
Correct: A physical walk-through is the only way to be certain no child has been left behind.
Incorrect: A child may not notice or may give an incorrect answer; the driver is solely responsible.
Incorrect: Mirrors have blind spots, and a child could be slumped down out of sight.
questions.explanation: The most reliable 'child check' procedure is for the driver to physically walk the length of the bus after each run, checking every seat. Many school districts have policies that require drivers to place a sign in the rearmost window after the check is complete to confirm it was done.

questions.question: You are securing a 20,000-pound piece of machinery on a flatbed trailer. What must be the minimum aggregate working load limit (WLL) of your tie-down system?
answers: 5,000 pounds
10,000 pounds
20,000 pounds
40,000 pounds
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is insufficient.
Correct: The aggregate WLL of all securement devices must be at least 50% of the weight of the cargo.
Incorrect: While a 1:1 ratio is excellent, the minimum requirement is 50%.
Incorrect: This is excessive and not required.
questions.explanation: According to FMCSA's cargo securement rules (§393.106), the combined working load limit of all tie-downs used to secure an article of cargo must be at least one-half (50%) of the weight of the article. For a 20,000 lb piece of machinery, the aggregate WLL must be at least 10,000 lbs.

questions.question: How do you recover from a drive-wheel braking skid?
answers: Push in the clutch to disengage the engine.
Steer into the skid and continue to brake hard.
Stop braking, turn the steering wheel quickly in the opposite direction of the skid, and then counter-steer.
Stop braking to allow the drive wheels to start rolling again, then counter-steer to bring the vehicle back in line.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This will not help regain traction and removes the ability to use the engine to help recover.
Incorrect: You should not continue to brake hard.
Incorrect: This describes a more complex and potentially incorrect recovery.
Correct: The first step is to get the wheels to stop skidding by releasing the brake. Then you can steer to recover.
questions.explanation: A drive-wheel braking skid occurs when the drive wheels lock up under braking. The rear of the vehicle will begin to slide out. To recover, you must first release the brakes to allow the wheels to unlock and regain traction. Then, you must steer in the direction you want to go (counter-steering away from the skid) to straighten the vehicle.

questions.question: The air brake system's safety valve is set to open at what pressure?
answers: 100 psi
125 psi
150 psi
200 psi
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the typical cut-in pressure for the compressor.
Incorrect: This is the typical cut-out pressure.
Correct: The safety valve protects the system from excessive pressure and is set to a higher level than the normal operating range.
Incorrect: This pressure is too high and would indicate a severe system malfunction.
questions.explanation: The safety valve is a non-adjustable valve, usually set to open at 150 psi, which protects the air tanks and the rest of the system from over-pressurization in case the governor fails to cut-out the compressor. If this valve releases air, it's a sign that the system needs immediate repair.

questions.question: When are you allowed to transport Division 1.1 explosives and detonators in the same vehicle?
answers: Under no circumstances.
If they are separated by a distance of at least 25 feet.
If they are in separate, DOT-approved containers.
If the detonators are in a Type 2 or Type 3 magazine and separated from the explosives, often by a hardwood wall of a specified thickness.
feedbacks: Incorrect: There are specific, highly regulated exceptions.
Incorrect: A specific distance is not the rule; the type of separation matters.
Incorrect: The container alone is not sufficient.
Correct: 49 CFR §177.835 specifies strict requirements for transporting different types of explosives together, allowing for separation by approved magazines or compartments.
questions.explanation: While generally forbidden, transporting blasting caps (detonators) with other explosives is allowed under very strict conditions outlined in 49 CFR §177.835. The regulations detail the construction of special vehicle compartments or the use of approved portable containers (magazines) to ensure the detonators cannot sympathetically detonate the other explosives.

questions.question: According to the CVSA Out-of-Service criteria, which of these tire conditions would place your vehicle out-of-service?
answers: Tread depth on a front steering tire is 3/32 of an inch.
The tire is audibly leaking air.
The tire pressure is 10% below the manufacturer's recommendation.
The tire has been repaired with a plug on the sidewall.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The minimum for a front tire is 4/32, but being under is a violation, not necessarily an OOS condition unless it's 2/32 or less.
Correct: An audible air leak from a tire is an automatic out-of-service condition.
Incorrect: While this should be corrected, it is not an OOS violation unless it is 50% or less of the maximum inflation pressure.
Correct: Plugs in the sidewall are not a proper repair, and this is considered an unsafe condition.
questions.explanation: The Commercial Vehicle Safety Alliance (CVSA) maintains the Out-of-Service (OOS) criteria used during roadside inspections. Any audibly leaking tire or an improperly repaired tire (such as a sidewall plug) makes the vehicle unsafe to continue its trip and will result in an OOS order.

questions.question: You are driving a passenger bus in California and begin to smell smoke. Which TWO actions have the highest priority?
answers: Immediately pull over to a safe location and stop the bus.
Call your dispatcher to report the situation.
Begin an orderly evacuation of all passengers.
Try to locate the source of the smoke while continuing to drive.
Use the PA system to ask if any passengers know first aid.
feedbacks: Correct: The first step in any potential fire emergency is to stop the vehicle safely.
Incorrect: While necessary, this is not a higher priority than passenger safety.
Correct: Once stopped, the highest priority is to get the passengers off the bus and to a safe distance away.
Incorrect: Continuing to drive could worsen the fire and endanger everyone.
Incorrect: This is not relevant to the immediate hazard of a potential fire.
questions.explanation: In a fire emergency, time is critical. The driver's absolute first priorities are to stop the bus in a safe place and evacuate all passengers immediately. All other actions, such as calling for help or attempting to fight the fire, come after ensuring the passengers are safe.
